style.vernacular: Swiss lake-and-river city: medieval Altstadt of narrow 3-4 storey eaves-to-street houses in plaster/whitewash and sandstone with steep clay-tile roofs; late 19th-century Gruenderzeit stone-faced blocks with mansard or hip roofs; interwar Neues Bauen and 1950s-70s concrete modernism; glass-and-steel offices in Oerlikon/Zuerich-West; surrounding villages and towns (Winterthur, Baden, Bremgarten, lake-side Pfannenstiel) of render houses with timber shutters, gabled/hipped tile roofs and baroque church towers with onion or spire helms. Tidy paved streets, lime and plane trees, conifers on the hills.
style.ornament: Shutters (Fensterlaeden) in green, red or grey beside punched windows; baroque onion-dome and pointed spire helms; oriel windows (Erker) and fresco painting on Altstadt facades; sandstone window frames and quoins; stepped gables; gilded clock faces and ball finials; modern concrete grids and large glazed fronts.

sources.what: Altstadt on both banks of the Limmat; Gruenderzeit building boom, 1930s Neues Bauen, post-1946 modern high-rises
Altstadt houses typically 3-4 storeys in unbroken rows with eaves to the street, Gothic and Baroque, oriel windows and frescoes on the Stadtturm
well-preserved old town on a ridge, Gothic and Baroque listed houses, neoclassical Rathaus
